lines.text: Why does sending a message to the other side of the planet take one second, but a bank transfer takes three business days?
It is not because the computers are slow; it is due to a fifty-year-old banking architecture called ACH.
The Automated Clearing House was designed in the nineteen-seventies to replace physical paper checks.
Instead of settling transactions instantly, banks bundle transfers into giant batches processed only a few times a day.
Transfers flow to the Federal Reserve, which verifies reserve funds and settles debits overnight.
The three-day lag also allows banks to catch fraudulent overdrafts, while earning interest on funds in transit.
New real-time networks like FedNow are finally bringing instant transfers into the modern age.
